// @camis:generated — do not edit; regenerated by camis
import type { NextFunction, Request, Response } from "express";

interface HttpError {
  status?: unknown;
  statusCode?: unknown;
  expose?: unknown;
  message?: unknown;
}

/** A stack's frames: its first line repeats the message. */
const frames = (stack: unknown): string =>
  typeof stack === "string"
    ? stack
        .split("\n")
        .filter((line) => line.trimStart().startsWith("at "))
        .join("\n")
    : "";

/**
 * What is logged of a failure. A database driver's error carries the statement and its values
 * (mysql2's `sql`, postgres-js's `parameters` and `detail`) and its message can quote a value it
 * refused, so of an error with a code only its name, its code and its frames are logged.
 */
const logged = (error: unknown): string => {
  if (!(error instanceof Error)) return "a value that is not an Error was thrown";
  const code = (error as { code?: unknown }).code;
  const what = code === undefined ? `${error.name}: ${error.message}` : `${error.name} (code ${String(code)})`;
  return `${what}\n${frames(error.stack)}`;
};

const clientStatus = (error: HttpError): number | undefined => {
  const status = error.status ?? error.statusCode;
  return typeof status === "number" && status >= 400 && status < 500 ? status : undefined;
};

/**
 * The last middleware, for an error a route or middleware hands on. A client error (express.json()'s
 * 400 for a body that does not parse, 413 for one too large) answers its message as JSON; any other
 * answers 500 with nothing of the error in it (no stack, query or path) and is logged on the server
 * without the values it carries.
 */
export const errorHandler = (
  error: unknown,
  _req: Request,
  res: Response,
  next: NextFunction,
): void => {
  if (res.headersSent) {
    next(error);
    return;
  }
  const details: HttpError = typeof error === "object" && error !== null ? error : {};
  const status = clientStatus(details);
  if (status !== undefined) {
    const exposed = details.expose === true && typeof details.message === "string";
    res.status(status).json({ error: exposed ? details.message : "bad request" });
    return;
  }
  console.error("request failed:", logged(error));
  res.status(500).json({ error: "internal error" });
};
